A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work by the same authors. The complete main texts, equations, two figures, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: v2 reports theoretical guarantees, proofs, and analytical examples. Its two figures are proof schematics; no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes appear in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 remains theoretical throughout, including its appendices. The added critical-radius proposition is a mathematical result, not an empirical study.

M1.justification: The standard and doubly regularized WDRO objectives, loss formulations, and dual representations are retained. No algorithm, model component, or training or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or tasks empirically. Regression, classification, clustering, and neural networks remain analytical examples of the framework’s applicability.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baseline comparisons. Expanded discussion of earlier theoretical work does not introduce experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Neither version specifies an empirical evaluation protocol. Sample-size conditions and radius choices concern mathematical guarantees, not experimental settings.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, or case studies. The analytical counterexample in v2 Proposition F.3 is retained as v3 Proposition F.4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, empirical uncertainty estimates, or significance tests. The probability bounds are theoretical statements, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are added, removed, or revised. The existing main bounds and linear-model constants are retained; the new formal characterization belongs to the theoretical changes.

T1.justification: v3 adds Proposition F.3 and its proof: under Assumption 2.1 and supp P = Xi, the critical radius is positive exactly when F contains no constant functions. Assumption 3.1.1 also explicitly adds omega >= 1. The central generalization theorems and existing proof architecture remain unchanged.

C1.justification: Both versions claim exact generalization guarantees with dimension-free radius scaling, coverage of nonsmooth losses, excess-risk bounds, and extension to double regularization. Revised introductory wording does not materially change these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix F.1 newly interprets the critical radius as a measure of loss fluctuations and gives a precise characterization under full support. v2 discusses positivity informally and emphasizes the degeneracy threshold. The limitations in Section 3.4 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Neither version provides computational implementation details, hardware specifications, training budgets, or code/data release instructions. Added notation and proof explanations do not change reproducibility information of this kind.

R1.justification: Section 1.3 distinguishes approximate from exact guarantees and expands discussion of Gao (2022); Section 2 elaborates restrictions in Azizian et al. (2023a). New references include Lee and Raginsky (2018), Bartlett and Mendelson (2006), Vapnik (1999), and Villani (2009). The central positioning relative to prior WDRO theory is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract and Sections 1.1–1.4 undergo substantial rewriting, reorganizing the opening narrative around exact versus approximate guarantees and their rates. Section 2 gains explanatory discussion, and supplemental notation is expanded. This is a substantial revision of the exposition, although the overall section sequence and most proof prose are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adopts the ICLR publication format, changing title styling, headings, running headers, reference layout, and text flow. Figures 1 and 2 retain their diagrams and captions but shift placement; Figure 2’s caption now spans pages. No figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v3 supplies a useful proof and explicit full-support qualification for the critical-radius characterization that v2 discusses informally. The revised introduction also makes the distinction between exact and approximate guarantees clearer. These improve precision and accessibility, while the central bounds, proof strategy, and substantive limitations remain largely unchanged.
